title: Custom session bucket minimums with enterprise security questionnaire onboarding trigger
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and run an experiment that replaces a flat per-account monthly minimum with per-session bucketed minimums and a questionnaire-driven onboarding flow for enterprise customers. The goal is to better align minimums with real session usage patterns (short interactive sessions vs. long generation jobs) and to automate exceptions for customers who require private deployments / additional security controls as captured in the Enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ).
background: Current hosted pricing enforces a single monthly minimum tied to aggregate tokens which disincentivizes low-latency interactive sessions and penalizes customers who have many short conversations. Sales frequently asks for explicit SQ-driven exceptions and credits when customers require VPC/private deployments or strict KMS policies. Previous experiments focused on directional IO floors and streaming minimums; this ticket proposes a session-first approach that maps to contractual onboarding flows.
proposal: Introduce session buckets (micro, standard, long) where each session is assigned a bucket by a heuristic (duration, output tokens, presence of streaming). Minimums are billed per active session bucket on a rolling monthly window with an account-level cap. Add an onboarding integration: when an enterprise fills the Security Questionnaire with evidence of private/VPC or HSM requirements, the system flags the account for automatic minimum waiver or adjusted bucket thresholds during the contract negotiation window.
experiment_design: Cohorts: Control (current monthly minimum) vs. Variant A (session buckets without SQ waivers) vs. Variant B (session buckets + SQ-driven waivers)

Bucket definitions: micro (<128 output tokens or <5s streaming), standard (128-2048 output tokens / interactive chat), long (>2048 output tokens or >60s streaming). Heuristics to be iterated in ENG spike.
Directional weights: bill = 0.3*input_tokens + 0.7*output_tokens for session normalization; test both 50/50 and 30/70 splits as sub-variants.
Billing behavior: Bucket minimums apply when an account has more than N sessions of a bucket type in a 30-day sliding window; cap lab: no account pays >2x previous-month baseline due to switching.

SQ Flow: When SQ indicates private deployment requirement, flag account and apply waiver policy for first 3 invoice cycles or until Dedicated/Private is provisioned. Legal must approve waiver template.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side feature flag session_bucket_experiment_v2 exists and can route accounts into control/variant cohorts
Heuristic service can classify sessions into micro/standard/long with >95% match on labeled sample set
Billing pipeline can apply per-session bucket minimums and enforce cap; no regressions in invoice generation for control cohort
SQ onboarding integration can be toggled and sets the waiver flag in the account record; waiver document template exists and is stored in Drive
Telemetry dashboard displays per-cohort ARR delta, churn, average revenue per session, customer complaints related to billing (tracked), and percent of waivers applied
Legal and Compliance sign-off on waiver workflow and data retention for SQ artifacts
metrics: Delta MRR attributable to minimum changes (cohort-level)
Churn rate for low-usage accounts (target no uplift > 0.5% absolute)
Number of support billing tickets per 100 accounts (target < 2x control)
Avg tokens per session by bucket, distribution shift after rollout
Percent of enterprise SQs resulting in waivers and time-to-waiver (days)
rollout_plan: Week 0: ENG spike to validate session classification heuristics and estimate computational cost
Week 1-2: Implement classification in runtime proxy + feature flag targeting; billing-side prototype to simulate monthly invoices
Week 3: Internal pilot with 10 accounts (mix of low/med/high usage) and sales-informed customers; collect feedback and disputes
Week 4-6: Expand to 5% of active hosted accounts as experiment; enable SQ waiver path for enterprise leads only
Week 7: Evaluate metrics; prepare decision doc (scale, iterate, or rollback).
risks: Complexity in billing migration could cause mis-invoicing — mitigate with shadow billing for 2 cycles
Customers will try to game session classification (artificially open sessions) — add heuristics to ignore idle time and rapid reconnects
Sales/legal may require manual exceptions increasing operational load — provide a simple waiver UI and a TTL on waivers
SQ data sensitivity — ensure SQ artifacts are stored in approved S3 bucket with KMS and limited access
notes: This ticket deliberately avoids changing per-token list price; experiment focuses on minimum structure and allocation rules
Prior experiments showed directional IO weighting reduces variance for multi-turn chat; we will reuse those telemetry queries
Discussed with Solutions Eng (Rosa Kim) about mapping waiver criteria to contract clauses; Rosa will own sales enablement doc
